summary: Describes the graphics equipment at NASA's Ames Research Center in 1971, such as plotters, storage-tube displays and an IBM 2250, with more devices planned. Because the devices were so varied, Ames was building a device-independent package. It answers a request that sites describe their graphics environments.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 126 lists graphics devices at NASA Ames and describes a package being built to support them. A device-independent language describes a picture, then the package converts it into commands for the selected device.

subtitle: Graphics equipment at Ames and a package for describing pictures across devices.

tldr.problem: Ames has graphics devices from different manufacturers with different software support and device commands.
tldr.mechanism: The package describes a picture in a device-independent intermediate language and converts it into orders for the selected device.
tldr.outcome: The note lists current and near-future graphics equipment and asks other sites to describe their graphics environments.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 126 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC describes graphics facilities and a package then being implemented at Ames.

sections.title: Graphics Devices at Ames
sections.content:
The note lists the graphics facilities at Ames for the IBM 360/67 TSS: an SC 4020 off-line microfilm system, Calcomp plotters, ARDS storage-tube CRTs, IMLAC PDS-1 refresh CRTs and one IBM 2250 CRT.

It says an Evans and Sutherland LDS-2 system and Hazeltine alphanumeric CRTs are expected to be in use in the near future.
sections.plainLanguage: Ames has several kinds of graphics equipment, including plotters, display tubes and CRTs. The note also lists two types of device expected soon.

sections.title: A Device-Independent Picture Language
sections.content:
Because the devices differ and their manufacturers provide varying software support, Ames is implementing a device-independent package. Its basic element is an intermediate language that describes the picture to display.

When a device is selected, the package converts that description into the specific device orders.
sections.plainLanguage: A program describes the picture without naming a particular machine. The package translates that description into commands the selected device understands.

sections.title: Subpictures and Network Sharing
sections.content:
The package also supports defining and storing subpictures for later use in more complex pictures. The note says an interface has been specified so graphic data sets can be transmitted to other installations on the TSS network.

McConnell asks other sites to describe their graphics environments and their thoughts on using graphics with ILLIAC IV when it becomes a functioning node at Ames.
sections.plainLanguage: Stored subpictures can be reused to build more complex pictures. The note also describes a way to send graphic data sets to other TSS installations.
